claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake and drop an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, before it ever starts.
In `SUPERSEDED` mode, if a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each run in turn.
CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline type.
The AWS CLI `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set `executionMode` and `pipelineType` for a pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
The link to AWS CodePipeline docs concepts-how-it-works page describes CodePipeline execution mode.
The registry page /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/ exists for aws.codepipeline.Pipeline.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that can prevent concurrent deployment runs targeting that environment.
An exclusive lock check is added from the Azure DevOps environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, the `lockBehavior` property can be set on a stage that references an environment with an exclusive lock check.
The default value of `lockBehavior` in Azure Pipelines is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting are passed over (cancelled) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack one at a time.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource for managing the exclusive lock check as code.
Link targets exist: /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ and /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
The page links to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ as the update conflict documentation.
TeamCity's advanced build configuration option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0 (unlimited).
The TeamCity option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' is located under the build configuration's General Settings.
With the TeamCity limit set to 1, a second build that would otherwise start immediately is queued behind the first and runs only after it finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease gives the same one-at-a-time behavior for updates to a stack.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job serializes deployments to that environment.
In Azure Pipelines, the stage-level setting `lockBehavior: sequential` is used together with an exclusive lock check so runs queue sequentially.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 on the build configuration serializes deployments.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
